skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate and refine AI videos using inference.sh CLI examples for text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar lipsync, upscaling, foley, and clip merging.
skill.summary: Guide AI video generation workflows across Veo, Seedance, Wan, Grok, OmniHuman, Fabric, and utility models.
skill.author: inference-sh-8

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are Markdown backtick false positives or documented infsh examples. The quick start contains a real curl-to-sh installer pattern and hardcoded installer URL, which are unsafe for automatic trust. No prompt-injection text or additional semantic malware intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl piped to sh with manual download, checksum verification, and an explicit installer command.

remediation.issue: Remote installer trust depends on an external domain
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and checksum in the skill documentation or link to signed release artifacts.

remediation.issue: Examples upload media URLs to a remote service
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to avoid sensitive media and confirm uploads to inference.sh before running CLI commands.

content.value_statement: AI video tasks require matching prompts, models, and CLI options. This skill guides inference.sh video generation, animation, lipsync, upscaling, and media merging.
actual_capabilities: Lists text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar, lipsync, foley, upscaling, and merge models.
Shows infsh CLI commands for Veo, Grok, Wan, OmniHuman, Fabric, PixVerse, Topaz, and media merger.
Guides users to browse all video apps with the inference.sh CLI.
Provides example inputs for prompts, image URLs, audio URLs, video URLs, transitions, and foley prompts.
Links to inference.sh documentation for running apps, streaming results, and media workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, account access, and network connectivity.
Media inputs and generated outputs are sent to the inference.sh service.
Model availability, cost, speed, and output quality depend on the remote provider.
The quick start installer uses pipe-to-shell and should be reviewed before use.

use_cases.title: Draft Marketing Clips
use_cases.description: Create short concept clips, product teasers, and campaign visuals before commissioning final production.

use_cases.title: Prototype Avatar Lessons
use_cases.description: Plan talking-head lessons or narrated explainers from approved portraits and audio.

use_cases.title: Finish Generated Media
use_cases.description: Upscale clips, add foley effects, or merge generated scenes into a simple sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend a text-to-video model and prepare a safe command for a 5 second clip about [topic].

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose an image-to-video model for [image URL] and define motion, camera style, duration, and quality settings.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Avatar Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse for a talking-head video using approved image and audio assets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a workflow that generates scenes, adds foley, upscales clips, and merges them into one final video.

output_examples.input: User asks for a five-second forest drone shot with audio.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Veo 3.1 Fast, drafts a concise prompt, and notes that the CLI will contact inference.sh.

output_examples.input: User has a portrait and narration audio for a training clip.
output_examples.output: The skill compares avatar and lipsync models, then suggests approved asset URLs and privacy checks before generation.

output_examples.input: User wants to finish two generated clips.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests foley, upscaling, and a fade transition workflow using the media utilities.

best_practices: Review remote installer commands before running them.
Use approved media URLs and avoid confidential images, voices, or unreleased footage.
Choose the smallest model and duration that can validate the creative direction.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts directly into a shell.
Do not upload private portraits, voices, or customer media without consent.
Do not assume placeholder URLs in examples are production-ready inputs.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose inference.sh video models and prepare CLI workflows for video generation and finishing.

faq.question: Does it generate videos locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI and remote model providers to create or process videos.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What must be installed first?
faq.answer: Users need the inference.sh CLI, account access, login, and network connectivity.

faq.question: Can it use image and audio inputs?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported models accept approved image, audio, or video URLs for animation, avatars, lipsync, and finishing.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The quick start uses a remote installer piped to a shell. Review and verify installer steps before running commands.
